description: Sign in to Telegram, find chats by name, read bounded history, and send plain or native HTML messages (--format plain|html) for the owner with an idempotent send ledger.
configHelp: Chat-first setup: the user is in this chat, so ask and show everything here. 1. Run `codeterm plugin telegram-client health`. If its state is `not-installed`, run the returned `installCommand` exactly; it downloads the pinned tg v0.11.0 release, verifies its SHA-256, and installs it into this instance's plugin runtime directory (`runtimeDir`). Run health again. 2. Ask the user in chat for their Telegram API ID and API hash. They create them at https://my.telegram.org → API development tools → create an application (any App title and Short name, platform Desktop; URL and description may stay empty). 3. Store each value from stdin only: `printf '%s' '<API_ID>' | codeterm plugin config telegram-client --secret api_id` and `printf '%s' '<API_HASH>' | codeterm plugin config telegram-client --secret api_hash`. Never use `--set` for them, never pass them as arguments, and never echo the hash back. 4. Run `codeterm plugin telegram-client login`. If it returns an error, show it in chat and ask the user for corrected credentials. On success it returns `qrSvg` (a ready QR image), `qrPayload` and `tgLink`: render `qrSvg` in chat inside an `html` block (or write it to an .svg file in your pad and show it with `@ct-image ABSOLUTE_PATH`) and print `tgLink` as text. Ask the user to scan it in Telegram Settings → Devices → Link Desktop Device. 5. Poll `codeterm plugin telegram-client login-status` and act on its `next` field: `show-qr` renders the returned `qrSvg` (a different one means a fresh QR); `wait` polls again; `done` means signed in, so confirm with `codeterm plugin telegram-client health` and `codeterm plugin telegram-client accounts`. 6. When `next` is `ask-password` (state `password-required`, `passwordRequired: true`), the account has two-step verification: ask the user in chat for their Telegram cloud password, show `step.hint` if present, and submit it from stdin only: `printf '%s' '<PASSWORD>' | codeterm plugin config telegram-client --secret login_password && codeterm plugin telegram-client login-password`. login-password reads and deletes that one-shot secret immediately and passes it to tg only through its process environment. Never put the password in a command argument, a file, or a log, and never repeat it back. Tell the user before they type it that a password sent in chat stays in this provider's session history, and offer the private alternative: the Telegram Client view shows a masked password field for the same step. Then keep polling login-status: `ask-password` again with `step.retry` true means Telegram rejected it; `show-qr` means the pending sign-in expired, so render the new QR and the password is applied automatically after the scan. 7. When `next` is `unsupported-step`, Telegram asked for something the pinned tg cannot take non-interactively (`step.prompt` names it); tell the user and send them to the Telegram Client view. `fix-credentials` means Telegram rejected the API ID or hash: ask for corrected values and store them again. Sending for the owner (e.g. "send Anna Ivanova: test"): 1. Run `codeterm plugin telegram-client chats <name>` (name or @username; users, groups and channels). If `match` is set, use its `id`. If `ambiguous` is true, list `candidates` (title, @username, type, id) in chat and ask the owner which one; if there is no match, ask for a more exact name. Never guess between candidates. 2. Run `codeterm plugin telegram-client send <id> --key <unique-key> <text>` with a fresh key per message the owner asked for (for example `tg-` plus a timestamp), and reuse the same key only to retry that same message. Use `--format html` explicitly for HTML markup; plain is the default and leaves tags literal. `--format markdown` returns invalid-request and sends nothing because the pinned client has no Markdown parser. HTML parse errors return `invalid-markup:` with the exact client message. 3. Report the result: on `status: sent` tell the owner it was sent and give `telegramMessageId`. On `unknown:` say Telegram may or may not have received it, never call it delivered, and do not resend with a new key unless the owner asks after checking the chat. On `chat-not-allowed:` the owner turned on Restrict agent sends in the Telegram Client view; relay the message, which names the setting. `chat-not-found`, `rate-limited`, `reauth-needed`, `not-logged-in`, `upstream-rejected` and `invalid-request` say what to fix. `preview <id> <text>` is an optional dry run that shows the resolved recipient without sending. Ask the owner only when the chat is ambiguous; do not ask for a separate confirmation of a message the owner already dictated. Agent verbs: `accounts`, `use <account-id>`, `chats [query]`, `history <chat-id> [n]`, `health`, `logout`, `login`, `login-status`, `login-password` (stdin secret only), `preview <chat-id> <text>`, `send <chat-id> [--key <idempotency-key>] [--format plain|html|markdown] [--] <text>` (alias `send-to`; default plain; html uses native tg --html; markdown is refused because pinned tg has no native Markdown parser). History is capped at 50 messages and 32 KiB. API credentials reach tg through its process environment, never arguments; tg keeps app_hash in its YAML config inside the plugin runtime directory. On macOS sessions use the login Keychain; other platforms keep a session file in the plugin runtime directory.
